claim: In the 5 July 2016 Gongbatongshacuo GLOF, the flood front propagated between seismic stations 28-35 km below the Zhangzangbo confluence at 8.7 m/s, with a slower second (coarse-sediment) pulse at 5 m/s.
stance_target: fast (~50 m/s) near-source celerity decaying to 6-7 m/s as a universal law; supports 5-9 m/s mid-reach
quoted_support: The first is the flood front, which propagates between stations at 8.7 m/s. ... The second pulse is of higher magnitude but travels slower, at 5 m/s.

claim: GLOF peak discharge attenuates downstream until it crosses monsoon-flood magnitude.
quoted_support: As a GLOF travels downstream, the flood peak attenuates and the peak discharge decreases, whereas the drainage area and background discharge increase
